primary_claim: On Llama-3.3-70B, injected 'subconscious' (outside-the-J-space) concept vectors are never verbally named by the model (0% naming rate at rank r=2000) even though they causally shift the model's output logits (+13.7 to +21.1 nats uplift for the injected concept token), while Anthropic's Natural Language Autoencoder (NLA) reads these same subconscious concepts almost perfectly (100% at r=2000) with zero false positives across every control tested.

effect.metric: concept-naming rate: model self-report (P(yes)/verbal naming) vs NLA readout, at rank r=2000
effect.value: model names conscious (J) component 80% of the time and subconscious (non-J) component 0% of the time; NLA names both components ~100% of the time with zero false positives across controls

depends_on: arXiv:2509.13316 (Li et al., privileged-information control critique)
contradicts_or_qualifies: Replicates and extends Anthropic's J-space paper's measured workspace fraction (6-7% on Claude) with the first open-weights replication on Llama-3.3-70B (6.1% J-energy at r=200), and further finds the workspace boundary is not a clean wall but a spectrum spread across thousands of directions, so the clean self-report/NLA divergence only appears once rank is swept up to r=2000 rather than the paper's r=200
stated_future_work: Try NLAs on situations with natural (non-synthetic) activations, such as line counting, language planning, and eval awareness
Use better NLAs trained on techniques from 'Building Better Activation Oracles', with multi-layer/higher FVE, to surface more cognition
limitations_stated: The NLA is still prone to confabulation, e.g. inventing context like the 'Batman franchise' or 'dragons' for some injections, or naming only a general idea (e.g. 'a specific emotion') without the exact concept

Injecting random directions inside J-space produced a higher P(yes) (0.077-0.095) than real concept vectors' J components (0.038), showing P(yes) alone is not a reliable introspection signal, which is why the analysis relies on whether the model verbally names the concept instead
A preliminary line-counting test found the NLA does not surface the exact character count that the J-lens/model can, showing the methods can miss different kinds of content
quote: The model names the conscious part 80% of the time, and the subconscious part never, even though the subconscious side carries 70% of the vector's energy and shoves the concept token's logprob up to +21.1 nats on every trial.
